newsitem.title: USA: Simpson defense team used deception, lawyer claims.
newsitem.headline: Simpson defense team used deception, lawyer claims.

text.p: A lawyer for the plaintiffs in O.J. Simpson's civil trial on Tuesday accused the former football star's legal team of using deception and dishonesty in defending him against a wrongful-death lawsuit.
"They tried to distract you. Their whole defence has been deception, desperation, dishonesty," attorney Tom Lambert told the panel in the plaintiffs' rebuttal argument.

Simpson was acquitted in 1995 in the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman. The current lawsuit, brought by the families of the victims, seeks substantial damages for the loss of their loved ones.

Simpson's attorneys have tried to show that evidence in the case was planted, that it was contaminated by sloppy laboratory work and that the police bungled their investigation of the June 12, 1994, murders.

But Lambert said the DNA test results on blood evidence found at the murder scene where the victims were stabbed and slashed to death and at Simpson's mansion two miles away were "extremely significant evidence establishing the guilt of Mr Simpson."

Lambert said the only DNA witness brought on by the defence, Dr. John Gerdes, had agreed that the test results were significant and had only questioned one blood spot at the murder scene as being possibly contaminated.

Court proceedings started 90 minutes late after attorneys for both sides met with Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki in his chambers followed by a one-hour recess. There was no immediate explanation for the delay.
The jury was expected to get the case for deliberation by the end of the day.
